newsitem.title: UK: Labour says will bring down UK government any way.
newsitem.headline: Labour says will bring down UK government any way.

text.p: The leader of Britain's opposition Labour Party, Tony Blair, said on Monday an election was needed as soon as possible to restore firm government and his party would bring down the Conservative government any way it could.
"As the government staggers on, we will seek to bring it down any way we can, in accordance with national interest and proper parliamentary procedure," he said in a New Year message.

Blair said 1997 was the year in which the Conservative government would have to face the people's verdict. Prime Minister John Major, now heading a minority administration, must call national elections by May.
"Britain needs a general election as soon as possible to restore firm and coherent government," Blair said.
"I believe that when the prime minister finally calls an election, the people will choose new Labour," he added.

Blair said that if he became prime minister he would establish a new partnership with business and industry, extend educational opportunity, be strong in Europe and put in place the foundations of a modernised welfare state.
He said the British people were looking to new Labour for "leadership, for a renewed sense of purpose and direction, and for hope".
"I am confident we can rise to the challenge. We have changed and the people know those changes are real and lasting," Blair said.
